title: I thought my sister died carrying one last secret to her grave.

blocks.text: For fifteen years, I had hated my sister.
Not the kind of hatred that burns loudly.
Her birthday disappeared from my calendar. Her calls went unanswered. Her Christmas cards went unopened. When relatives mentioned her name, I changed the subject.
And when she died three weeks ago, I didn’t go to her funeral.
My name is Claire Mercer, and fifteen years earlier, I came home early from a business trip and found my husband, Daniel, kissing my younger sister, Natalie, in our bedroom.
Within six months, my marriage was over.
She moved to another state. Daniel disappeared from my life.
It wasn’t easy, but eventually I met someone else, bought a small house, and learned how to live without asking why my own sister had betrayed me.
Then, fifteen years later, Natalie died giving birth to a baby girl.
“Claire, please come home. She was asking for you.”
“She’s been dead to me for fifteen years,” I said.
The next morning, someone knocked on my door.
It was a gray-haired attorney I’d never met.
“I’m sorry, but I don’t want anything from her.”
My name was written across the front in Natalie’s handwriting.
I hadn’t seen her handwriting in fifteen years.
It showed Natalie sitting in a hospital bed, exhausted but smiling.
A little girl wrapped in a yellow blanket.
“What does my daughter have to do with Natalie?”
He slid another document across the table.
My daughter Emily had been born fifteen years earlier.
What I didn’t know was that Natalie had been listed as the emergency contact.
“Because Natalie wasn’t just your sister, Claire.”
“She was involved in something you were never told about.”
Claire, I know you believe I destroyed your marriage. I didn’t. Not the way you think.
After fifteen years, she was still making excuses.
She wrote that the night I caught her with Daniel had been deliberately staged.
He had discovered something about Emily’s birth and threatened to expose it unless Natalie helped him convince me that she had betrayed me.
Fifteen years earlier, shortly before Emily was born, doctors discovered that Daniel was not biologically capable of fathering a child.
The information was supposed to remain confidential.
But Daniel became obsessed with knowing who the donor was.
She discovered the identity accidentally.
And the donor was someone neither Daniel nor I had expected.
I stared at the page for nearly a minute.
My father had died years before Emily was born.
Martin explained that my father had privately donated genetic material before a medical treatment that later made him infertile.
Then came the part that shattered everything.
He threatened to tell me that Emily wasn’t his biological child.
That’s when he created the scene I had witnessed.
He told Natalie that if she didn’t cooperate, he’d destroy our family.
Daniel had forced it as part of his plan.
I sat on my kitchen floor holding the letter.
My entire life had been built around a lie.
But there was one thing I couldn’t understand.
He showed me copies of letters Natalie had mailed to me.
Daniel had been arrested thirteen years earlier for financial fraud.
During the investigation, his belongings were seized.
Among them was a box containing my sister’s letters.
“This was written the day Natalie went into labor.”
If I don’t survive tonight, please forgive me. I know I don’t deserve it, but I need you to know that I never betrayed you.
I protected Emily because I promised you I would.
But there’s something else you don’t know.
I’d raised her believing Daniel was her father.
I’d never told her why her aunt had disappeared.
“She found me online. She told me she was sick. She said she didn’t know if she would get another chance.”
“She said the person who helped bring me into this world wasn’t a stranger.”
Martin was still sitting across from me.
He seemed to know exactly what was coming.
